parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM .mjs, manual argv parsing, no npm dependencies, jsonschema Draft7Validator/ErrorTree behavior, and output in /output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent wrote shared infrastructure and stubs, then split six keyword modules across children while reserving final integration for itself.
parallel.implementation: Children produced split keyword files; several implemented local workarounds after discovering framework or helper mismatches, and one child edited validator.mjs outside its module.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Files were side-effect written into the shared output tree, but the parent timed out as the swarm returned and did not reconcile child reports or run final integration.
parallel.verification: Each child ran local differential suites, but verification was uneven: some reported unresolved mismatches, one test harness was contaminated, and no parent-level whole-program check followed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed 0/60; the run timed out, one child was aborted, and shared equality/framework issues remained unadjudicated.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, no-dependency, manual argv, jsonschema behavior, ErrorTree, and /output file hierarchy requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned probing, implementation, integration, CLI, meta-schema, keyword logic, and final delivery without delegation.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote pytypes, pyjson, errors, errorTree, metaSchema, keywords, validator, argparse, and test18.mjs as one coherent codebase.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial kept all edits in one implementation path, removed its temporary harness, listed final files, and produced a completion response.
serial.verification: Serial ran an 86-case differential suite, extra argument parsing and stress checks, and reported byte-for-byte local matches and exit-code matches.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite stronger closure, the current official evaluator also reports 0/60, with no per-test failure detail mounted to isolate the exact defect.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the prompt's ESM, .mjs, no-dependency, CLI, and jsonschema behavior requirements before creating the framework and stubs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and explicitly listed the final module hierarchy as pure ESM with zero external dependencies.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was similar, but serial carried it to a final completed response while parallel ended before final acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split keyword families to six children after the parent wrote shared infrastructure and told children to edit only assigned modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, implementation, and verification under one actor and tracked the work through a local todo list.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained concurrent module work but introduced child lifecycle and shared ownership risks; serial avoided those boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave children common helper and validator contracts, but child reports show equality and framework assumptions became contested across module boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built value semantics and keyword behavior in one design, then summarized strict bool-number equality and ErrorTree dedup behavior together.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's component interface assumptions needed cross-agent reconciliation; serial's single owner kept those semantics centralized.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a shared validator skeleton, six keyword files, and child-local patches/workarounds including a logical child edit to validator.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote pytypes, pyjson, a combined keywords module, validator, parser, and entry point in one sequence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's path was distributed and partially conflicting; serial's path was monolithic and internally consistent though still officially wrong.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The swarm ended with five completed children and one aborted child, and the parent turn was cancelled at the same boundary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran tests, cleaned up, updated todos to done, and emitted a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did not complete result inspection or adoption after the child phase; serial closed the result lifecycle explicitly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote to the same /output tree and /tmp area; one child consumed another's /tmp script and another modified shared validator infrastructure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one harness under /output, removed it, and listed final files without concurrent workspace actors.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had concrete shared-state contamination and cross-file provenance issues; serial had a single owned shared state lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child-local tests were numerous but uneven, with unresolved mismatch reports and no parent-level end-to-end verification after the swarm.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran an 86-case differential suite, extra argument and stress checks, and reported local byte-for-byte matching before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had a coherent acceptance pass; parallel had fragmented local evidence and no whole-task acceptance before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full cell budget, status reports timed_out true, and the prompt outcome did not complete.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 1061 seconds, did not time out, and left 1336 seconds of budget in status.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent the budget before final integration; serial had ample closure time, though the official score was still failing.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both current completed evaluations failed 0 of 60 tests. The concrete task-solving difference is process closure. Serial completed a unified implementation and local differential acceptance loop, while parallel delegated modules, encountered shared-state and cross-file coordination issues, lost one child to cancellation, and never ran the parent-level final integration it planned.
parallel_contributors: The swarm returned at timeout with five completed children and one aborted child, preventing normal parent-level integration.
Equality semantics and validator framework behavior were changed or bypassed across files without a single reconciled design.
Temporary test artifact leakage contaminated at least one child verification pass.
serial_contributors: Serial kept ownership centralized and ran local differential, argument, and stress checks before final response.
Serial removed its test harness and delivered a single coherent file list.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel child reports themselves document unresolved numeric precision and regex semantic limitations.
Serial local verification did not predict the hidden official 0/60 outcome, so ordinary implementation gaps likely remained despite local tests.
evaluator_effects: Only aggregate official pass counts are mounted; no per-test official failure log is available in the isolated pair.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative process contributors; no unique official-score root cause because both modes fail and detailed evaluator cases are unavailable

candidates.reason: The parallel parent launched six implementation children, but the array child was explicitly cancelled while its active fuzz/verification turn was running, and the swarm result recorded one aborted child. The serial run had no child lifecycle and completed its local differential suite and final response.
candidates.realized_consequence: One required keyword-module implementation/verification stream lost its final handoff, and the parent closed by timeout with no post-swarm integration pass.
candidates.near_match_reason: The same episode includes no later parent decision point after a returned failure; the directly observed event is the orchestration cancellation/interruption itself.

candidates.reason: There was no complete mutually compatible component set ready for final promotion; one child was aborted and other modules reported unresolved limitations.
No parent-level integrated verification occurred before later integration; child-local tests were not the final acceptance checkpoint.
Completed child work was written into the shared output tree as side effects; the principal lifecycle failure was the aborted child, not an unjoined completed implementation.
No verifier-only child produced a concrete result trapped below the parent; the missing result belongs to the cancelled implementation child chain.
The cancelled child left no later parent recovery window because the parent turn itself was cancelled at timeout; Early Child Termination is the more direct label.
Completed child reports were returned only at the terminal cancelled swarm result; no later parent decision point ignored a visible completed result.
The parent waited on the swarm, but the direct evidence is the child cancellation/result boundary rather than available progress ignored during a live decision window.

The parent created a shared equality/type helper contract, then different children implemented or bypassed equality semantics in their own keyword files after discovering the shared helper was wrong. Those cross-file implementations claimed the same semantic surface and required reconciliation that never occurred before timeout.
candidates.realized_consequence: The final parallel tree contained unreconciled equality behavior across the shared helper and keyword modules, leaving global validator semantics unreviewed as a single design.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent did provide file and signature contracts; the concrete adverse event was competing cross-file implementations of the same equality behavior, not a wholly absent interface contract.

candidates.reason: The logical child edited parent-authored validator.mjs, but no simultaneous same-file edit or observed same-file reconciliation race is shown.
No non-entry source was deleted, recreated, or wholesale overwritten by another actor; the concrete retained write issue is cross-file semantic overlap.
No actor replaced the submitted entry point while another actor owned or used it.
There is no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing multiple final outputs.
Shared /output writes existed, but the more specific retained source problem is cross-file scope collision around equality semantics.

The numeric child created a generic temporary differential script, and the logical child later copied and ran that path as if it were its own test harness. The resulting numeric mismatch contaminated logical verification until the child diagnosed the clobber and rewrote tests under a unique name.
candidates.realized_consequence: Logical-keyword verification consumed a wrong temporary artifact, produced an irrelevant failure, and required rework before meaningful logical tests could run.
candidates.near_match_reason: The contaminated object was a temporary test harness consumed as input, not a source-file write collision in the final implementation workspace.
